name: CardiacLens v9.10.347.207
notes: HOTFIX for a real regression in v9.10.347.206. Disabling the duplicate 'Takeover' lock-screen system in .206 exposed a genuine, previously-hidden layout bug in the original keyboard: 30 keys arranged in a 4-column grid produced 7 rows, the last with only 2 keys, and the full grid ran 70-90px taller than a real iPhone's visible screen. This had been there for months but was always covered by Takeover's overlay rendering on top of it, so it was never actually seen or tested on a real device until .206 removed that overlay. The overflow made large parts of the keyboard unreachable, which is the most likely explanation for lock/unlock feeling broken or inconsistent in real use even though the underlying tap-handling logic (fixed in .206) was correct. Fixed: grid changed from 4 columns to 5, so 30 keys divide into exactly 6 even rows instead of 7 uneven ones. Confirmed by direct measurement on both a standard iPhone (390x844) and iPhone SE (375x667) viewport size, not estimated from CSS alone.

This release does not change any unlock/lock logic, only the grid's column count. The fixes shipped in .206 (Takeover disabled, async rebuild race closed, fluid notification routing) are unchanged and still in effect.
label: SecureAccessGridOverflowHotfix
summary: Hotfix: the Secure Access keyboard grid did not fit on a real iPhone screen after v9.10.347.206 exposed a previously-hidden layout bug. Changed from 4 to 5 columns so all 30 keys fit in 6 even rows within the visible screen.
fixes: Secure Access keyboard grid changed from 4 columns (7 uneven rows, overflowed the screen) to 5 columns (6 even rows, fits the screen).
testing: Root cause found by direct measurement in real headless Chromium (pre-installed at /opt/pw-browsers) at real iPhone viewport sizes: prior to this fix, grid bottom edge measured 897px and 843px against visible viewports of 844px and 667px respectively (iPhone 13/14 and iPhone SE) -- genuinely overflowing on both. After the fix, grid bottom edge measured 756px and 632px against the same viewports -- fits with margin on both, and all 6 rows confirmed to hold exactly 5 keys each (no uneven row).

Re-ran a full real-browser pass after the fix: (1) grid fits and rows are even -- confirmed by measurement; (2) a real M/purple/purple/purple tap sequence via actual .click() on the actual rendered buttons genuinely unlocks the app; (3) changing the Secure Access combination through the real Settings UI (real button clicks, real dropdown selection, real text input) and reloading the page confirms the new combination survives the reload -- localStorage after reload matched localStorage before reload exactly. Zero uncaught page errors across the full sequence.

Correction to this session's own process: an earlier reload-persistence test incorrectly appeared to show Settings saves reverting after reload. That was traced to a mistake in the test script itself (Playwright's add_init_script re-fires on every navigation including reload, which was silently re-seeding old values at the moment of reload) rather than a real app bug. Corrected the test methodology and re-verified: Settings saves for Secure Access do genuinely persist across a real reload, through both the Settings-panel edit flow and the first-time 3-step setup wizard.

Not tested: an actual physical tap on a real iPhone touchscreen. Real DOM clicks in a real browser at real iPhone viewport dimensions were used as the closest available substitute in this environment.
